final.label: workaround-needs-tracking

skill_entry.name: 14. A workaround for an unexplained defect needs a tracked exit
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, in the diff's added lines under h/, src/ or t/, in this PR's own commit messages, or in the PR body: (a) a comment or commit message calls a behavior a workaround (workaround, work-around, hack) and says the cause is unknown (unidentified, unexplained, not understood, 'root cause is an open question', 'See TODO' with no id after it); (b) a TEST_CASE or SECTION that the diff adds, or adds assertions to, whose header comment (the comment lines between the unit's opening line and its first statement) says the unit guards or protects a workaround, a hang avoidance, or an ordering 'required for production hardware'; (c) a commit of this PR declares a helper obsolete for a named hardware or firmware version ('No longer necessary with 1.5.7.0', 'fixed in bitfile X') while another helper for the same defect (zero, clear, scrub, NaN) survives in t/ or in the files the diff touches.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE is the merge-base against the PR's base branch (gh pr view N --json baseRefName), not origin/main. 2. Grep the added lines (h/ src/ t/ only), this PR's commit messages and the body for workaround and unknown-cause words. An unknown-cause hit counts only with a workaround word within 15 lines of it or in the same commit message; a .md or doc/ hit never counts. 3. Classify each hit: UNEXPLAINED (cause unknown), NAMED-DEFECT (defect named), PROVISIONAL ('for now' about a size, default or ordering, no defect), REMOVAL. 4. Per UNEXPLAINED hit: search the 31-line window, the oldest commit that added the phrase, and the body for a tracker id; a body id closes the hit only inside a workaround paragraph. 5. Per triggered test unit: the header must state permanent contract plus a consumer, or a TODO plus the condition that replaces the test; an id in the TODO is optional. 6. Per obsolescence commit: list surviving sibling helpers, their TRON_*_WORKAROUND gate and whether a build file defines the macro.
skill_entry.question: Is this workaround temporary or permanent? If temporary, which story tracks the root cause, and where does the test say what replaces it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: NAMED-DEFECT workarounds: a defect name alone passes in silence (tron-2008 'as a workaround for DMA/NOC issue' with no owner and no exit, tron-2135 'Until we get a fixed bitfile', both approved with no text; tron-2302 'temporary workaround ... present in the latest bitfile' drew only a comments ask, 3036997452). A removed workaround (tron-2011). A bare TODO without an id: origin/main h/ src/ t/ carries 133 TODO/FIXME/XXX lines and only 4 carry a tracker id. An id-less TODO that states the replacement condition (origin/main:t/t_heap_v2.cpp:244). A pre-existing unit at HEAD that cites a workaround and the diff does not add or widen (t/t_hwattention.cpp 'transfer_k_and_v' at the heads of PRs 2475, 2875, 3756, 4353, all silent). A workaround commit that belongs to another PR on the same side branch. A tracker id inside an explanatory Note (3350285744 asks to remove it). Gate polarity against the commit message (comment-contradicts-adjacent-code owns it). He never asks for the root cause before merge ('No harm it leaving it').
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<function>` (<file>:<line>) is described as a workaround for a bug nobody has identified, and `<TEST_CASE name>` (<test>:<line>) pins that behavior. do we have a ticket/story tracking this for follow up? If it is temporary, say so in the test with a TODO and the condition that replaces it; if it is permanent, name the consumer and drop the word workaround. Obsolescence variant: with <version> that fixed <defect>, `<helper>` (<file>:<line>) should not be needed anymore; no harm leaving it, but is it gated so it can be dropped?
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: A plain question with no severity word for the missing tracker ('do we have a ticket/story tracking this for follow up?', 'so are we enshrining this work-around forever?'); the author changed the test the same day (3227468540 at 14:58Z, e4c4f49452 at 18:18Z). A self-note for the obsolete helper ('No harm it leaving it, but I have a to-do to circle back'), nit level; the author still gated it (958e77d919, reply 'fixed in commit 958e77d91' the next morning). Never blocking; he approved both PRs (ab8a7f758b 2026-05-18, 8e19ea3e62 2026-03-18).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the workaround comment), other files (the guarding test under t/ for a production comment under src/), commits (the commit that added the workaround and any commit of this PR that declares a sibling helper obsolete for a version; the version-fixed-defect claim is read from that commit message, no hardware knowledge is needed), PR body (tracker ids, read per paragraph), build files (whether any defines a TRON_*_WORKAROUND macro); no CI or runtime evidence needed.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a workaround for an unexplained defect needs a tracked exit

Setup for this check: the PR's base branch, not origin/main. `BASEREF=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$BASEREF)`. On PR 2713 origin/main gives 426 commits and 42 step-1 hits; origin/hwattention_sync gives 20 commits and 10 hits. `gh pr view N --json body -q .body > body.md`.

1. Hits, three sources.
   a. Added code lines, already as HEAD file:line: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3)} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]; next} /^\+/{print f":"n": "$0; n++}' | grep -i -E 'work-?around|\bhack\b|unidentified|unexplained|not understood|root cause|open question'`. Do not add `for now` or `until the` to this grep; they matched only ordinary comments (t/t_heap_v2.cpp:502, t/t_token_tree_refcount.cpp:87, tron-1722 x5, PR 4596 x3). Limiting to h src t removes the design-spec 'Open questions' headings under doc/.
   b. This PR's commit messages, each hit prefixed with its commit id: `git -C WT log --format='COMMIT %h %s%n%b' --no-merges BASE..HEAD | awk '/^COMMIT /{c=$2} /work-?around|unexplained|root cause|open question|no longer (necessary|needed) (with|in|on|since) |fixed in (bitfile|firmware|release|v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)/ {print c": "$0}'`. Keep only commits of this PR when the side branch carries other PRs: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/<sha>/pulls --jq '.[].number'` must list N.
   c. Body: `grep -n -i -E 'work-?around|pending (a |the )?(fix|bitfile|firmware)|until (we|a|the) .*(bitfile|firmware|fix)|bitfile [0-9]' body.md`; record the paragraph of each hit.
2. Classify each hit. Mechanical rule first: a hit on an unknown-cause word (unidentified, unexplained, not understood, root cause, open question) counts only when a workaround word (work-?around, hack) appears within 15 lines of it in the same file at HEAD (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L-15)),$((L+15))p" | grep -i -E 'work-?around|\bhack\b'`) or in the same commit message. Classes: UNEXPLAINED = the text says the cause is unknown. NAMED-DEFECT = the text names the defect (a component or bus such as DMA/NOC, a bitfile or firmware version, an issue id, a hardware state such as post-power-cycle); an owner or exit condition is welcome but not required. PROVISIONAL = a 'for now', 'temporarily' or 'until' about a size, default, ordering or test scope with no defect named; never continues. REMOVAL = a removed line or a commit that drops a workaround. Only UNEXPLAINED continues at step 3; REMOVAL and obsolescence commits continue at step 5.
3. Tracker search per UNEXPLAINED hit at HEAD line L of FILE. Window: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L-15)),$((L+15))p" | grep -n -E 'STORY-[0-9]+|[A-Za-z_]+#[0-9]+|#[0-9]{3,}|notion\.so/|/issues/[0-9]+'`. Adding commit: `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' -S'<distinct phrase of the comment>' BASE..HEAD`; when a fixup reworded the comment several commits return, take the oldest (last line) and read it with `git -C WT log -1 --format=%B <sha> | grep -n -E '<id pattern>'`. Body: the same id grep over body.md, but an id closes the hit only when it sits in a paragraph that step 1c matched; an id elsewhere names another item (on PR 2713 body.md:1 'STORY-425' is the fragmentation story, step 1c matched 0 paragraphs, so the heap_v2.cpp:293 hit stays). No id anywhere = finding (a question).
4. Guarding tests, diff test files only (never all of t/ at HEAD; the whole-tree form returned 7 pre-existing hits in 4 untouched files on PR 2713 and fires on four silent PRs): `git -C WT grep -n -i -E 'work-?around|silently flipped|\bhang\b|required for production' HEAD -- $(git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- 't/*')`. Enclosing unit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /TEST_CASE\(|SECTION\(|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\(/ {n=NR; name=$0} END{print n": "name}'`. A unit counts only when the diff adds it or adds assertions to it, or when its body calls the helper that a step-2 UNEXPLAINED hit describes; a comment above a helper function is not a unit header. Header range: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | awk -v S=<unit start> 'NR>=S {print NR": "$0} NR>S && /REQUIRE|CHECK/ {exit}'`. Required: either a 'permanent contract' sentence with a named consumer (then check 1 owns the row), or `TODO` plus the condition that replaces the test (`grep -c -E 'TODO'` and read the sentence). An id inside the TODO is optional; the id must exist where the reviewer can read it (body paragraph, review reply, commit message). A header with neither sentence = finding.
5. Obsolescence, per step-1b commit that says a version fixed a defect. Sibling list from what the commit removed: `git -C WT show <sha> | grep -o -E '^-[^/]*\b[a-z_]*(clear|zero|scrub|nan)[a-z_]*\b' | sort -u`, plus the defect word from its message (NaN, hang, DMA); then `git -C WT grep -n -i -E '<those stems>|clear_|zero_|zeroi[sz]e|scrub' HEAD -- h src t`. Gates: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'TRON_[A-Z_]*WORKAROUND' HEAD -- h src t CMakeLists.txt t/CMakeLists.txt nix flake.nix CMakePresets.json GNUmakefile`. For each survivor record whether a gate wraps it and whether any build file defines the macro. Do not grade the directive against the commit message here; a message that says 'compiles out by default' over an `#ifndef` is a comment-contradicts-adjacent-code finding.
6. Report one question per step-3 miss, one per step-4 unit, one nit per step-5 survivor ('no harm leaving it, but is it gated so it can be dropped?') with its gate and definition site.

On PR 2713 (reviewed commit 25d146aa15, BASE 4bc2416b05 against origin/hwattention_sync, 20 commits): step 1a gives 4 code hits (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:293 'Reproducible workaround for an unidentified bug', :302 'See TODO: open question for follow-up', t/t_heap_v2.cpp:226, :230); step 1b gives 05a5f1e787 x2 and 32e7c3d6be x3 ('Root cause is an open question'); step 1c gives 0. Step 3: 0 ids in :278-317, 0 in 32e7c3d6be, body id STORY-425 outside any workaround paragraph -> question (3227447122; author answered STORY-445). Step 4: t/t_heap_v2.cpp:224 TEST_CASE 'expand: first allocation comes from the lowest-offset hugepage', header :226-231 'Guards the workaround in expand()', first REQUIRE :237, CHECK(p == chunk_base) :242, no TODO -> finding (3227468540); e4c4f49452 added the TODO(STORY-445) block the same day, present at the approved commit ab8a7f758b:t/t_heap_v2.cpp:235; 18ad29da06 (2026-08-18) dropped the id, origin/main:t/t_heap_v2.cpp:244 reads 'TODO: replace with a test for whatever invariant the root-cause investigation establishes', which passes step 4. Step 5 did not trigger (0 obsolescence commits). On PR 2176 (review commit 9553cd0a11, base hwattention_sync): step 1b hits d3e1020563 'remove shard::zero_v_hbm. No longer necessary with 1.5.7.0' (gh api commits/d3e1020563/pulls lists 2176; an ancestor of 9553cd0a11); the merge-base-vs-origin/main form returned 8 hits, 5 from PRs 2135, 2008 and 1827. Step 5: survivor clear_kv_hbm at 9553cd0a11:t/t_hwattention.cpp:63, called :544, no TRON_*_WORKAROUND gate -> nit (2948238427); 958e77d919 then wrapped it in `#ifndef TRON_NAN_FPGA_WORKAROUND` (429249ead6:t/t_hwattention.cpp:63, :545-548) with no definition in any build file at 429249ead6 or origin/main (8f0243118b); origin/main:t/t_hwattention_2.cpp:270, :434, :618 use `#ifdef` for the same macro.
final.widen_delta: None (new check 14). Cross-references: a workaround row that the test calls a permanent contract goes to check 1 (consumer); the enclosing-unit awk is check 5 step 2; a tracker id or story number inside an explanatory comment or Note is the code-comment widening of check 9 / code-comment-carries-no-lasting-fact (3350285744), not this check; a commit message that claims 'compiles out by default' over an `#ifndef` gate is comment-contradicts-adjacent-code; a gated helper that skips on CI hosts is check 3. The common setup line `BASE=$(git merge-base $HEAD origin/main)` in procedures.md needs the baseRefName form for every check, because 15 of the 48 silent PRs and PRs 2713 and 2176 target hwattention_sync; this check states it locally until the common setup is changed.

quotes.quote: do we have a ticket/story tracking this for follow up?
quotes.what_it_shows: The whole ask for an unexplained workaround: a tracking item, in question form, no severity word; the hunk said 'workaround for an unidentified bug' and 'See TODO: open question for follow-up' with no id (ff19045fd0:src/system/heap_v2.cpp:339, 2026-05-12).

quotes.quote: so are we enshrining this work-around forever? Or will be create a story to pursue/understand/address it further? If so we should probably call that out here with a TODO or something.
quotes.what_it_shows: A test that pins a workaround must say whether it is permanent or temporary; the remedy is a TODO in the test plus a story, not dropping the test (ff19045fd0:t/t_heap_v2.cpp:234, 2026-05-12).

quotes.quote: I'm really hoping that with the 'NaN-fixed' bitfile, we don't need this 'clear_kv_hbm' anymore. No harm it leaving it, but I have a to-do to circle back and see if we can skip this. Once things settle ;-p...
quotes.what_it_shows: The obsolescence variant: a hardware fix named in the same PR makes a sibling helper suspect; severity is a self-note ('No harm it leaving it'), yet the author gated it (958e77d919, 2026-03-18).
The contrast: a tracker id inside an explanatory Note is unwanted; the id belongs with a TODO that marks temporary behavior, or in the PR thread (2026-06-03).

quotes.quote: I know this is a pretty simple routine, but I'm a fan of comments :). Can you add some brief comments about what this is doing/how, and how to use `TRON_POISON_BITS`?
quotes.what_it_shows: Negative space: a workaround tool whose body says 'temporary workaround ... present in the latest bitfile' (cause named, exit condition named) drew a comments ask, not a ticket ask (2026-04-05).

final.precedent_note: n = 3 comments over 2 PRs (tron-2713: 3227447122, 3227468540; tron-2176: 2948238427), 2026-03-17 to 2026-05-12. No member is pasted assistant text: none of the three bodies contains 'Claude' or 'assistant', and PRs 2176 and 2713 are not in the CONTEXT.md pasted-text list (2233, 2461, 2872, 2906, 3008, 3490, 4128, 3879, 4191). The two contrast quotes (3350285744 on PR 2906, 2026-06-03; 3036997452 on PR 2302, 2026-04-05) are not members; PR 2906 is in the pasted-text list, but 3350285744 is a suggestion block in Wade's own words with no pasted text. Both member PRs are FPGA hardware workarounds by one author (bham0n); the obsolescence variant rests on one comment.
changes_made: Setup: BASE now comes from the PR's base branch (gh pr view N --json baseRefName) instead of origin/main; both member PRs target hwattention_sync (verified with gh pr view 2713 and 2176). Step 1b keeps only this PR's commits (gh api commits/<sha>/pulls). Folded from PRECISION and EXECUTABILITY, which agreed.

Step 1a: diff grep limited to h src t, output mapped to HEAD file:line by an awk over the @@ headers; 'for now' and 'until (we|a|the)' removed from the primary grep (EXECUTABILITY's command, PRECISION's word list).

Step 1b: commit grep emits the commit id per hit (EXECUTABILITY's COMMIT awk) and uses PRECISION's narrower patterns 'fixed in (bitfile|firmware|release|version)' and 'no longer (necessary|needed) (with|in|on|since)'. Step 1c body pattern narrowed to workaround/pending-fix/bitfile forms (PRECISION); 'temporar|pending' alone dropped (tron-2875 'pending listeners', tron-4353).

Step 2: added EXECUTABILITY's mechanical rule (an unknown-cause word counts only with a workaround word within 15 lines or in the same commit message; .md and doc/ never) and PRECISION's four classes with NAMED-DEFECT requiring only a named defect (tron-2008 has no owner and no exit and was silent) and a new PROVISIONAL class.

Step 3: a body id closes a hit only inside a step-1c paragraph (EXECUTABILITY; on PR 2713 STORY-425 would otherwise suppress 3227447122); the -S commit search takes the oldest commit when several return.

Step 4: grep restricted to the diff's test files, a unit counts only when the diff adds or widens it or its body calls the UNEXPLAINED helper; the trigger (b) rewritten so a helper-function comment (t/t_clearhbm.cpp:38 at PR 2475) is not a unit header. Both refuters agreed. On the id requirement they disagreed: PRECISION makes the id optional, EXECUTABILITY keeps 'TODO(<id>) count 0 = finding'. Decided for PRECISION: origin/main:t/t_heap_v2.cpp:244 (verified) carries an id-less TODO with a replacement condition after 18ad29da06, and the literal count fires on every head after 2026-08-18 (PRs 3756, 4353). The id must exist where the reviewer can read it (body paragraph, reply, commit message).

Step 5: the polarity clause (compare #ifdef/#ifndef with the commit message) deleted; PRECISION asked to delete it, EXECUTABILITY kept the gate grep as written, FACTS showed the three #ifdef asks (PR 1920) are about debug dumps. Decided for PRECISION: 0 of 243 inline comments support it and comment-contradicts-adjacent-code owns a message-versus-code mismatch. The gate grep and the definition-site check stay. The sibling-helper list is now derived from the symbols the obsolescence commit removed plus its defect word (EXECUTABILITY) instead of the PR 2176 symbol list.

do_not_fire: added the pre-existing 'transfer_k_and_v' unit at the heads of PRs 2475, 2875, 3756, 4353; the id-less TODO at origin/main:t/t_heap_v2.cpp:244; another PR's commit on the same side branch; gate polarity handed to comment-contradicts-adjacent-code. Corrected '133 TODO/FIXME/XXX lines and 1 tracker id' to '133 (whole-word) lines and only 4 carry a tracker id' (verified: host_matvec.hpp:167 #4366, force_generate.cpp:307 /issues/299, gemma_4_a4b_generation.hpp:59 TODO(#4352), t_mwaitx.cpp:178 /issues/1516; STORY-689 at src/runtron.cpp:304 is in an explanatory comment, not a TODO line).

Facts corrected in the On-PR lines: the PR 2713 test header is :226-231 (line 232 is 'pos_heap_v2 h;', verified); the t/t_clearhbm.cpp:39 sentence 'rather than an understood fix' is bf162628d7 (Brian Hamon, 2026-08-18), only :78 (originally :43) is Wade's 05b6ac0549 text (verified by git blame); the 't_clearhbm' and '67 digests' code_facts items are not carried into the entry, their corrected content lives in do_not_fire and precedent_note (the only inline tracker asks are the two PR 2713 comments; 3350285744 is the contrast hit; review bodies 4373886636 and 4800935083 say 'follow up' about review comments, not workarounds).
evidence_scope: 'hardware knowledge' replaced by 'the version-fixed-defect claim is read from the commit message' (EXECUTABILITY); build files added for the macro definition check.
severity_wade_uses: added the verified timing (3227468540 at 2026-05-12 14:58Z, e4c4f49452 at 18:18Z; author reply 'fixed in commit 958e77d91' 2026-03-18 01:47Z) and the approval commits.
widen_delta: added the note that procedures.md common setup uses origin/main and needs the baseRefName form for every check.
residual_risks: Corpus width: both member PRs are FPGA hardware workarounds by one author (bham0n); the obsolescence variant rests on one comment (2948238427). No corpus evidence shows how Wade treats a software-only unexplained workaround or a workaround by another author.

Where the tracker id lives stays contested inside the project: Wade asked for a story and a TODO (3227447122, 3227468540) and writes ids into his own workaround comments (origin/main:h/pos/device.hpp:746-747, llm_fpga#340), but rejects story numbers in explanatory Notes (3350285744), and the author removed STORY-445 from the test TODO (18ad29da06). The check demands the story exist and the test say the guard is temporary; it does not demand the id in code. If the user wants the id in the TODO, step 4 fires on every head after 2026-08-18 (PRs 3756, 4353 probed).

The expand() comment in src/system/heap_v2.cpp never received an id (origin/main:365-374) and Wade did not follow up; the acceptance bar observed is the author's reply plus the test TODO. A reviewer who treats the production comment as the finding site will ask again on every PR that touches heap_v2.cpp; step 4's diff-file restriction limits this to PRs that touch the test.

NAMED-DEFECT now requires only a named defect, so a workaround with a named defect and no exit condition passes (tron-2008 removed the exit clause 'should be reduced once we have an updated bitfile' and was silent). A reviewer may still want the exit condition; the corpus says Wade does not.

The fixed step 4 was reproduced on PR 2713 by reasoning over the refuters' probes (the 2713 unit is new in the PR, so the diff-file restriction keeps it); the folded commands were not re-run end to end on PR 2176 under the baseRefName setup. PRECISION's probe states d3e1020563 is listed under PR 2176 by gh api, so step 1b keeps it, but that single call was not repeated here.

Step 5's sibling-helper derivation from removed symbols is new text with no probe behind it; on a commit that removes no symbol (a message-only obsolescence claim) the stem list is empty and only the generic 'clear_|zero_|zeroi[sz]e|scrub' grep runs.
The common setup in procedures.md still says origin/main; until it is changed, agents running other checks on a hwattention_sync PR get the wrong BASE, and this check's local override may be missed.
